title: Crying and joy together: the soul's preparation for contemplation

lectures.id: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3
Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3
Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

overview: Chapter 6 asks what a person must have in his heart before he takes up the contemplation the book teaches. Its answer is that he needs both sorrow and joy: sorrow at being far from G-d, and joy in being close, arising together from the same contemplation, as the Zohar says, with tears on one side of the heart and joy on the other. Each must be real and deep. Joy alone breeds callousness, sorrow alone breeds despair, and feelings held only on the surface prepare nothing. The chapter then climbs the levels. Joy comes from understanding, *bina*, while the pleasure of *chachma* is a delight beyond understanding that produces *bittul*. Above both is the essence, which no mind grasps, and the tears there come from the wonder of that distance. Pleasure and pain, joy and sorrow, are one force in two equal poles, so the sorrow at G-d's absence is exactly proportional to the joy of His presence. The chapter ends with *tikun chatzos*, the midnight tears that prepare prayer, and with *prikas ol*, the casting off of the yoke, which is the root of sin.

sections.title: Tears and joy together: the preparation for contemplation
sections.summary: Before a person can take in the order of the worlds, his soul must be ready. The Zohar's image of tears on one side of the heart and joy on the other says he needs both: sorrow at being far from G-d, and joy in being close.

phrases.he: (ו) והנה ידוע המאמר דבכיה תקיעא בלבאי מסטרא דא וחדווה מסטרא דא כו'
phrases.en: It's known what it says in the Zohar, and it's quoted in Tanya, that tears or sorrow are wedged in my heart on one side, and joy, happiness, are in the other side.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: להיות שצריך להקדים בחינת הכנה בנפש לכללות הידיעה האלהי״ת בהשתלשלות דאור אין סוף באבי''ע עד שתהא הנפש בחינת כלי מוכן לזה
phrases.en: that a person needs to make this preparation, they have to prepare themselves emotionally and in their priorities before approaching the whole general subject of knowing G-d by studying the *seder hishtalshelus*, *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, so that the person's soul, which in this term is kind of the idea of a person's motivation and their priorities, are going to be proper and be a fitting vessel for this.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: וזה אינו אלא על ידי אמצעות ב' דברים הללו דבכיה וחדווה
phrases.en: And this preparation of the soul can only be accomplished through these both, the combination of and the balance of these two things, both.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: גם שהן ב' הפכים הרי באים כאחד ממש מהתבוננות אחת דווקא
phrases.en: even though seemingly they're two opposites, but they really come as one, and from the very same *hisbonenus* is really going to create both of these feelings.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The chapter opens by restating the work so far. The book has taught how to contemplate: first the general ideas, then the details and examples, then the balance of attitude, the drive for mastery joined to a sense of wonder at what lies beyond us. Now the chapter turns to priorities. A person has to sincerely want to know G-d, and then everything he learns falls into place. Someone with other interests gets distracted, like the traveller on the road to the king's palace who stops at every diversion. The chapter also touches on *teshuva* and on the month of Elul, which is near.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 048 opens with a recap of chapters 1 to 5 and of this chapter's theme; it is placed before line 1, where the class starts reading.

blocks.text: The chapter begins with the saying of the Zohar, quoted in Tanya: sorrow is wedged on one side of the heart and joy on the other. Tanya says that to succeed in prayer one must first arouse sorrow at being distant from G-d. In older generations people did this every day before prayer, with a seriousness and a longing to come close. It is hard now, so one sets aside special times for a *cheshbon hanefesh* (a reckoning of the soul), such as Thursday nights, and the month of Elul.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: This is one of the first things Tanya does, in its first chapter: it sets up that change and motion come from tension. If a person is happy where he is, he stays where he is. He has to feel that he wants to be somewhere ahead and that he is unhappy where he stands. Even wanting to be somewhere else is not enough, since one can stay comfortable and not bother to move. So both feelings are needed.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: That is why Tanya sets up at once that we are promised to be a *tzaddik*, that every person has that potential and it is demanded of us, and yet we should consider ourselves a *rasha*. We are not living up to that, and the tension is what starts a spiritual journey. Contemplation has to be born of the same two feelings: unhappiness at being far from G-d and wanting to come close, together with joy at the chance to come close. Those two together make a change that lasts. Without both, a person stagnates, gets distracted, or grows lazy.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The preparation must come before the whole subject of knowing G-d through the chain of worlds, so that the soul is a fitting vessel. Otherwise a person won't feel he needs it, and why would he bother? That is why Tanya starts by agitating us. Moses at the burning bush said, "Let me turn away from here and go there." A person needs that dissatisfaction, the turning from bad toward good. *Daas* is vital to understanding something, and it comes only when a person feels the knowledge is valuable and relevant to him. If he feels no lack and has no aspirations, he will not be motivated. Feeling a lack, together with joy in the accomplishment, is what makes it stick.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The preparation comes only through the two together. Though they are opposites, they arise as one from the same contemplation: one may be in the forefront and the other behind, but both are created at the same time.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: ובזה נעשה דווקא בחינת הכנה רבה בנפש לקבוע בעצמיות שלה מכל השגות פרטיות דאור אין סוף באבי''ע
phrases.en: And specifically when a person has these two feelings, that is what prepares the soul, makes a great preparation of the soul so that whatever the person understands of all these g-dly concepts and all the details of the *seder hishtalshelus*, *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, that it should all really be implanted deep within the person.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: ואם יחסר אחד מאלה
phrases.en: and if a person is missing or lacking one of these two sides, one of these two feelings,

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: דהיינו זה
phrases.en: which could be either that a person only has one without the other

phrases.he: בלא זה
phrases.en: they only have the sorrow without the joy, or only the joy without the sorrow

phrases.en: or even if a person imagines that he has both of these feelings in his heart, but they're not true and they're not deep.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: רק דרך מעביר חיצוני בעלמא,
phrases.en: they're just very passing external feelings.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: הרי זה סימן גמור שלא נקבע בנפשו כלום,
phrases.en: the fact that he doesn't have both of these feelings in a sincere, deep way is an absolute sign that nothing really penetrated to his soul.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: רק מרחוק מאד כו'
phrases.en: he's only viewing it from afar off.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: ובמעט דבר המנגד
phrases.en: and if a person lacks this deep connection, then even the slightest opposition,

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: כמו בטרדא גדולה
phrases.en: let's say they get very busy with things,

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: או בהרגשת עצמו ליש ביותר כו'
phrases.en: or if something comes to some aspect of their life where they feel ego and they feel that that, they feel very haughty about it,

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: ינתק מלבו לגמרי כו'.
phrases.en: then it will totally uproot all of these feelings.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: When the two feelings are real, the concepts of *Atzilus* and *Beriya* lodge in a person's self, and he is moved by them. When one feeling is missing, the result is one-sided. Joy alone, with a sense that it doesn't matter what I do, breeds callousness. Sorrow alone, always beating oneself up, breeds depression and giving up. Joy without the urgency that comes from feeling a lack gives no reason to act, so a person needs both.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Some people hold both feelings only on the surface, the way one studies for a test: he cares a little, passes, and forgets. Learning *chasidus* only to get the *mashpia* off one's back doesn't reach the core. The sign that nothing has sunk in is that the teaching stays external, a theory far off and not personal. The point is to find these ideas in oneself, to see that this is who I am. That gives a deep understanding and real enjoyment, and also a true sense of being disconnected from G-dliness.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: If a person lacks that deep connection, even a slight obstacle will uproot everything. He is in a *yeshiva* and goes with the flow, but when life gets hard, or he gets busy, or a bit of ego appears, he forgets it all. He is distracted, loses his love and fear of G-d, and may even sin. Only a priority that is the core of his life can overcome distractions and let him persevere. Without that, it is easily knocked over, and this is why it matters so much for our spiritual journey.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

sections.title: Why joy in G-d is hard: joy comes from grasping, and G-d cannot be grasped
sections.summary: Joy is born of understanding, *bina*, while the pleasure of *chachma* is a delight beyond understanding. The chapter then asks how joy can be in G-d's essence when understanding reaches only His handiwork.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים הנה ידוע דענג ושמחה הוא בחכמה ובינה, הענג בחכמה ושמחה בבינה
phrases.en: the explanation is, that generally speaking, pleasure and joy relate to *chachma* and *bina*, that pleasure comes from *chachma* and joy comes from *bina*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: (וזהו ההפרש בין שבת ליום טוב כידוע)
phrases.en: and this is the difference between *Shabbos* and *Yom Tov*, as is known,

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: כי ההשגה בשכל מוליד השמחה שהוא שמחת הנפש כמו שכתוב אם הבנים שמחה
phrases.en: so when a person understands something, you're struggling to understand it, and you grasp it, you've mastered it, you finish another chapter, you finish another book, whatever it is, that brings a person to the sense of joy, which is a joy of celebrating a sense of mastery and accomplishment; this is the joy of the soul, that it's understanding G-dliness, like it says, the mother of the children rejoices,

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: וידוע שעיקר השמחה דווקא באלהו״ת הוא, וכמו וישמחו בך דוקא
phrases.en: and it's known, that the main joy is actually in G-dliness, like it says in the verse, that we rejoice in You

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Pleasure and *simcha*, joy, both belong to *chachma* and *bina*, but in different ways. *Chachma* is the perception of what is beyond understanding, a direct experience that draws a person in, a delight that is essential and not tied to any achievement. *Bina* is a tangible joy from accomplishment, like winning or reaching a goal one set. In the teacher's simple terms: one is more of an *ein* (nothing), the other more of a *yesh* (something).

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Shabbos and Yom Tov show the same distinction. Yom Tov celebrates a particular accomplishment: Pesach its freedom and the barley harvest, Shavuos the giving of the Torah and the wheat harvest, Sukkos G-d's protection with the clouds of glory and the ingathering, the greatest joy. Shabbos is leisure: the essential pleasure of being happy to be alive, to have Torah, mitzvos and family, without celebrating anything in particular. So the pleasure of *chachma* is the Shabbos kind, and the joy of *bina* is the Yom Tov kind.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: When a person understands something after the struggle, he feels the joy of having mastered it, finishing a chapter or a book. With G-dliness that is the joy of the soul. As the verse says, the mother of the children rejoices, so *bina* is linked to joy.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The chief joy is in G-dliness: the greatest accomplishment is to feel connected to G-d, to fulfil a real mission, to bring out qualities in oneself or to help another bring them out. That is the joy of "we rejoice in You". The teacher says this could be explored at length, and it raises a question.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: ולפי הנזכר לעיל דבהשגה לית מחשבה תפיסא ביה, אדרבה מופלא בהפלאת הערך הנבדל כו'
phrases.en: but based on what we explained in the previous chapter, that in the realm of understanding of logic and reason, we said that no thought can grasp G-d, and so what we're understanding are His handiworks, but that's not really understanding Him, we're not really grasping Him. On the contrary, we said that recognizing G-d Himself is something that is transcendent and totally beyond anything, it defies human knowledge and human understanding.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: והיינו בבחינת כח מ''ה דחכמה בהעלם כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like we said, that's something that can only be perceived with the power of the *koach mah* of *chachma*, where we can have this recognition and direct experience of something that's beyond our understanding, which relates to *chachma*, not to *bina*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: ואם כן נהפוך הוא, שאין השמחה במהותו כו'
phrases.en: and so if so, it should be the opposite, that we're not actually having joy in G-d's essence seemingly. Seemingly we're having joy in His handiworks.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: כי מאחר שמשיג, אין זה אמיתתו ומהותו, רק בחינת צמצומו להוות המתהווה כו'
phrases.en: because it seems axiomatic that the very fact that you've understood something, that itself proves that it's not His true essence and nature. You're understanding just some external creation, or some external representation and expression of G-d, but not His true essence and nature, we're only understanding how G-d limits Himself to create the creations.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: ובחכמה, בחינת אין כנזכר לעיל, שם ראוי להיות השמחה, כמו שאמר וישמחו בך
phrases.en: but in *chachma*, which is this abstract type of connection, which allows us to have a direct experience of something beyond understanding, that's where we should have the joy, because that's where we're connecting to G-d, like we said before.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: ואינו כן כידוע, דהביטול היפך, השמחה בחכמה דווקא
phrases.en: this is not so, because the feeling, like we said, that *chachma* brings is a feeling of *bittul*, which is the opposite of joy, of being able to have a sense of accomplishment.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: והשמחה בבינה כו'
phrases.en: a person does not have joy from *chachma*, joy is through *bina*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: He does not answer it at once; first he lays out the ground.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.question: If joy comes from understanding, and understanding only grasps G-d's handiwork, how can the joy be in G-d's essence?

blocks.text: Joy in G-d's essence would have to come from *chachma*, where G-d is perceived beyond understanding. But *chachma* produces *bittul*, a sense of having understood nothing, which is the opposite of joy.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Chachma gives a feeling of bittul: a person sees how vast G-d's works are and feels he has understood nothing, which is a pain rather than joy. So joy comes through bina, and the question stands: how can there be joy in G-d's essence if the mind grasps only His handiwork, and the direct perception of Him produces bittul?

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

sections.title: Every thing has its opposite: one force, two equal sides
sections.summary: Everything has its opposite, and the opposite comes from the same force. Pleasure and pain are two expressions of one attachment, and they are exactly proportional. The example is meant to show the same for joy and sorrow.

phrases.he: אך הענין הוא כידוע שבכל דבר יש היפוכו, וגם שנגלה להיפוכו ממש,
phrases.en: so to answer, we have to first give a little introduction. It's known, that in everything you have its opposite, that you can have in a lot of things a certain type of relationship where it's like a two-dimensional thing, and it's expressed it can be expressed in two opposite ways, but those two expressions are really like two sides of one coin or they're both really coming from the same place.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: אדרבה מזה עצמו נראה לעין שכל כחו אינו בא רק מכח המנגדו ממש ולפי ערך כח המנגד כן ימצא כח היפוכו ממש, אם כן כדבר אחד ממש הוא
phrases.en: even though sometimes it can be expressed in its opposite, that actually shows us that its entire power comes only from its opposite. And however strong the opposing force is, that's exactly how strong you're going to have an equal and opposite force basically in these two directions. And so really those two sides are one, they're two sides of one coin, they're really the same thing, they're really one essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Everything has its opposite, and a thing can be revealed as its opposite. Even then, its force comes entirely from what opposes it. A thing and its opposite are two sides of one coin: the stronger the opposite, the exactly equal and opposite force comes out. So the two are really one thing and one essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: כמו הענג והצער,
phrases.en: for example, pleasure and pain.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: שלפי ערך כח התענוג בדבר מה, כן ממש לפי ערך ימצא כח התפעלות הצער, שהוא גרעון אור הענג המנגדו
phrases.en: that however much, how proportional to how much a person feels pleasure and enjoys something, exactly equal to that, proportional to that, the person will have the opposite and feel pain, which pain is the idea of the withdrawal of the light of pleasure which is opposing that pleasure.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: דהיינו אם יעמוד לנגדו דבר לבטל הענג ההוא להיות מן ההיפוך כו'
phrases.en: if something will stand before him to oppose him from getting what he wants and nullify that pleasure because it's the opposite of what he wants and what he enjoyed, he'll feel that proportional pain that he would have if he would have gotten it, the pleasure he would have had from getting it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: וכן להיפך, ערך הענג מדבר מה לא יוכר רק לפי ערך הצער בהעדר אותו הדבר כו'
phrases.en: and so to the opposite, the only way to really appreciate how much somebody enjoys something is by seeing the pain they have when they don't get it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: הרי כח אחד הוא ממש, רק שנחלק לב' קווין שוין ממש ושקולין
phrases.en: So, these two forces, the pleasure and the pain are really one force, they're one aspect of the soul. It's just that it's the expression of this singular idea, which is the attachment of yourself, the investment of yourself to something, gets divided in its expression to two opposite poles, which are equal, they're completely equal and completely proportional.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: בלתי יטה כח קו א' על ב' אפילו כקוצו של יו״ד
phrases.en: And they're completely evenly balanced, so that one will never be greater than the other, even to the tiniest amount, even like the horn of a *yud*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Pleasure and pain are two ways a person's attachment to something shows itself. The more he is invested in a thing and enjoys it, the more it hurts to lose it, and the two are exactly proportional, whether it is a prize, money, or anything he cares about. If something stands against his pleasure and cancels it, he feels the same pain that the pleasure would have given.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: We recognise how much we enjoy something by its absence. We miss the family when they leave, and a person in an uncomfortable situation forgets how much distress he is under until he gets relief.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: So pleasure and pain are one force, divided into two equal poles, balanced exactly, so that one is never larger than the other, even by the tip of a yud.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

sections.title: Crying and joy in equal measure, from the same attachment
sections.summary: Joy in revealed G-dliness and sorrow at its concealment are proportional. The same holds for redemption and exile, and for the core of each soul, which despises a life disconnected from G-d in proportion to its delight in G-d.

phrases.he: וכן החדווה והבכיה,
phrases.en: so too happiness and sorrow, or like laughing and crying,

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: שלפי ערך החדווה, שהוא ענג המורגש בגלוי אלקות בהשגתו כנזכר לעיל, כך ימצא קו הב' שיוצא ממנו ומכחו דוקא
phrases.en: that however much a person feels joy and pleasure and gladness from having this revealed pleasure of revelation of G-dliness, from grasp, from understanding it, or connecting to it, so equally so a person will experience the opposite, which derives from it, from the force of it, that he'll be distressed and feel sorrow and trouble for having a lack of G-dliness revealed in his soul.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: שהוא הבכיה על העדר גלוי האור בנפשו מצד הסתר אלהו״ת, עד שמואס בחייו ממש
phrases.en: proportional sorrow from a lack of G-dliness being revealed in their soul because G-dliness is being hidden to the point that a person will despise his life.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: *Chedva*, joy, and *bechiya*, sorrow, are the same pair. However much a person feels joy from revealed G-dliness, exactly that much he will feel sorrow at its absence. The same is true of redemption and exile: one who really rejoices in the *geulah* is pained by the *galus*, and on the personal level, by the exile of the *Shechinah* in his own soul. Each person is a microcosm of this. The more he appreciates G-dliness and knows it is his true identity, the more he despises a meaningless, disconnected life.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The Alter Rebbe's example: he offered a Chassid, Reb Isaac Hamiler, a long life, and the Chassid answered that it must not be empty years, with eyes that do not see G-dliness and ears that do not hear it. A prince forced to live like an animal would find that torture, since his whole life is bound to his father the king. So when a person feels that his soul's core is connected to G-dliness, a life full of Torah, mitzvos and spreading G-dliness brings him great joy, and the thought of an empty life is repulsive to him.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: The Alter Rebbe's blessing and the empty years

phrases.he: וכל שטעם טעם ענג אלה״י בחדווה יותר, יותר יתמרמר בנפשו מהיפוכו
phrases.en: the more a person tastes and experiences, once a person experiences this pleasure of G-dly joy, the G-dly happiness of living a G-dly life, the more that they will feel bitter and distressed from the opposite, from having an empty ungodly life.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: וכן להיפך,
phrases.en: and we have the opposite way, too.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: מערך עומק המרירות והבכיה למאוס בחייו הגשמים, ניכר ערך כח העונג והחדווה באלהו״ת, כמה ערך כוחו
phrases.en: that sometimes it's the opposite.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: כי ב' קווין הללו שקולין מאד בשווה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: because like we've explained, that these two polar opposites, these two sides are perfectly equal, they're exactly balanced.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: והיינו בכיה מסטרא דא וחדוה מסטרא דא בשקול אחד בשווה ממש
phrases.en: and this is what it means in the Zohar, that a person has both of these opposite feelings: the crying or the sorrow on one side of the heart, and the joy or the laughing on the other side of the heart, and they are equal, proportionate to each other.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The general rule: the more a person tastes G-dly delight, the more he recoils from its opposite. In Tanya, the true sign of a *tzaddik* is how much he despises evil. Enjoying G-dliness and still being drawn to what is bad shows he has not yet reached that level, because real love would pull him away from the opposite.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The reverse holds too. Someone who is pained by his inability to live a G-dly life, because he is cut off from the chances to learn and pray, shows by that pain that he would have great joy if he had them.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Maybe they are, G-d forbid, trapped in Communist Russia or something like that, or in some situation that keeps them from connecting to G-dliness.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

sensitivity.reason: Names a political regime (Communist Russia) as the example of a place where one cannot live a G-dly life; a public reader may take it as a political remark.
sensitivity.publishable: Maybe they are, G-d forbid, trapped in some place, or in some situation that keeps them from connecting to G-dliness.

blocks.text: The rest of the reverse case: the pain shows the joy. Whoever is repelled by the empty life and pained by its absence is showing that he would be joyful with the opportunity. So the two can go both ways.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The two are exactly equal: two sides of one coin. The question is how deep it is for the person, whether the attachment is an attractive thing separate from him or the core of who he is. When he finds that he is a piece of G-d from above, the sense of connection expresses itself in these two feelings in equal measure: both the love and the fear, the joy and the sorrow, the pleasure and the pain.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The teacher stops the first part here. The Mitteler Rebbe, he says, will show how the same phenomenon happens on the levels of *bina*, *chachma* and the essence of the *keser*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 048 ch 6 part 1.mp3

sections.title: Chachma and the essence: tears of what cannot be grasped
sections.summary: Above the joy of *bina* is the hidden delight of *chachma*, which brings a self-nullification (*bittul*) that is not a loss. Above that is the essence, where the mind cannot grasp, and the tears come from the wonder of that distance.

phrases.he: וכמו כן למעלה מזה בבחינת עונג הנעלם שבחכמה,
phrases.en: and the same thing applies to the higher than a higher level, which is this deep, like, subconscious pleasure or inner pleasure of *chachma*,

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: שמזה בא בחינת הביטול מעצמותו לגמרי,
phrases.en: this deeper type of connection of *chachma* brings a person to have this complete *bittul* where a person totally like goes loses themselves.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: (בל"א צו טראגן גאר פון זיך)
phrases.en: *tzu tragen gar fun zich*, it totally, like, takes somebody out of themselves.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: מעומק עונג הנעלם בעצמיות שלו כו'
phrases.en: and that's a much deeper type of pleasure which really is connected in a person's essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: הרי היפוכו הבא מכחו הוא ענין השלכת נפשו מנגד בכל דבר המנגד לזה,
phrases.en: the opposite effect of that, that comes from its force, is that a person is willing to basically have self-sacrifice and even give up their life for G-dliness, anything that's going to try to oppose this essential connection.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: שהוא נכלל בבחינת הרגשת עצמו
phrases.en: because this their connection to G-dliness is something that is completely part of their very sense of self.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: דהיינו למאוס בחייו בתכלית התבטלות האמיתית,
phrases.en: a person views their life that's disconnected from G-dliness as being totally disgusting and totally worthless to them, to the point where they'd rather die than give up their connection.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כמו מי לי בשמים ועמך כו'
phrases.en: like it says, what is there for me in the heavens, and with You I don't want anything on earth.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כלה כו'
phrases.en: my flesh and my soul expire for You.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כי ב' קווין שקולים בשווה הן כנזכר לעיל ודי למבין.
phrases.en: because these again, these two opposite feelings are completely equal and they're really two sides of one coin once again

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The class opens by picking up the middle of chapter 6: the balance of joy and sorrow, and the three levels, *bina*, *chachma* and the essence. Joy comes from *bina*, pleasure from *chachma*, and then the teacher goes higher to the essence. The recap is placed here, where the class goes on to the passage on *chachma*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Recap from the start of class 049 of lines 8 to 31; placed before line 32, where class 049 resumes reading.

blocks.text: Higher still is the hidden pleasure of *chachma*, which brings a complete *bittul* of the self. *Bina*'s joy is from accomplishments measured on a ladder: I did so many mitzvos, I learned so much. The delight of *chachma* is the intrinsic value of G-dliness, not any accomplishment: a person joys in having a G-dly soul and being part of everything created by G-d's will.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This delight makes a person feel his essential identity as a Jew, that he is G-d's child, and He is his father. That is more basic than what he does in Torah and mitzvos, and it is what we celebrate on Shabbos. It transcends any particular accomplishment. In Yiddish he says it takes a person totally out of himself: a much deeper pleasure, connected in his essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The opposite of this pleasure comes from its force: a person is willing to sacrifice himself, to give up his life rather than any opposition to this connection. This is the inherited love of G-d that every Jew has, which *Tanya* describes. Even without *hisbonenus* on the level of *bina*, a Jew is ready to die rather than give up his connection, and inner work can bring this to the front. The holiness of Shabbos is equal for all, because it does not depend on our level, but a certain contemplation is needed to reveal it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Such a person has a deep conviction that he would rather die than give up his connection. It is part of his very sense of self and his core identity, so it is not negotiable.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This is the idea that a person's life disconnected from G-dliness is totally disgusting and worthless to him, so that he would rather die than give up the connection. Like it says, "What is there for me in heaven? With You I don't want anything on earth." When a person activates this, through contemplation as the Alter Rebbe did, and through learning *chasidus*, he will not even want *Gan Eden* or the *olam haba*, only G-d Himself.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The motivation of *chachma* is to do what G-d wants, not to collect spiritual check-boxes. There are three general levels of serving G-d: from fear of reward and punishment; from competition and hierarchy, which belongs to the accomplishment of *bina*; and the deepest, doing it for its own sake, because one sees that his essential identity is a spark of G-d in him, with a mission of its own.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The two opposite feelings here are equal, two sides of one coin. A deep connection to G-dliness in the soul's core yields great satisfaction, and also great distress at being separate from G-dliness at all. That is the level of *chachma*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: והנה יש בכיה למעלה מזו, והוא הבא מהעדר ההשגה מחמת עוצם הפלאת והבדלת הערך, מפני שלא יכילו כלי מוחו כו'
phrases.en: there's a even deeper type of crying or sorrow than this, and this is where a person cannot understand and grasp G-d because it's essentially transcends the ability of the human mind to grasp and to understand.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כמו זלגו עיניו דמעות דרבי עקיבא בסודות עמוקות שלא יכיל הכלי כו'
phrases.en: like it says of *Rabbi Akiva*, when he was learning the secrets of the Torah, that his eyes were pouring tears because of the deep secrets that his mind could not contain.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: והוא בבחינת הפלאת סתימא דכל סתימין,
phrases.en: It's the hidden of all hidden things.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: דהיינו בעצמות אור אין סוף ממש אשר בלתי מושג כלל
phrases.en: the very essence of the *Ohr Ein Sof*, which is completely not understood or grasped at all.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: אדרבה, כל שיעמיק יותר, יותר יפלא כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: on the contrary, the more a person delves into understanding of G-dliness, the more they recognize that it's inherently beyond them

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: שמזה דוקא לבו דואג ובוכה.
phrases.en: that this very fact that it's beyond him and he can't, it's inherently impossible, that that causes him to be troubled, and he cries.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: שאינו בא רק מעוצם התענוג והתשוקה להשיג, ואינו יכול כו'
וידוע שזהו עיקר בחינת הכלי
phrases.en: this third level of being really desiring to know G-d's essence, and even though the more a person learns, the more he recognizes that it's beyond him, and that that itself bothers him, that is the main *keli*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: לבחינת חכמה ברזין דאורייתא
phrases.en: that type of motivation, and that type of intention is what makes a person a fitting receptacle to really receive the secrets of the Torah.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין אין מוסרין רזי תורה אלא למי שלבו דואג בקרבו כו'
phrases.en: like it's explained elsewhere about this teaching of our Sages, that the secrets of the Torah are only given to somebody whose heart is troubled within him.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: A deeper sorrow comes from not being able to grasp, from the *hafla'a*, the wonder, and the distance. The mind's vessel cannot contain it. Rabbi Akiva's tears over the deep secrets are the example: he was bothered that he wanted to understand and could not, and he knew it was beyond him.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This is the wonder of the hidden of all hidden, the essence of the infinite light, which is not grasped at all. The level of *chachma* is a perception of transcendence in direct experience, not in understanding. But here a person wants to grasp the essence, and cannot. The deeper he goes, the more it amazes him.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: That it is beyond him is what makes his heart worry and cry. The crying shows that he has the great pleasure and desire to understand, and that he is connected to the infinite light; he is withheld for now, and the Baal Shem Tov's saying applies: a person is where his desire is. The seraphim stand above the man on the chair, because their desire is to grasp G-dliness on that higher level. So the person who truly wants to be connected to the infinite light is connected there, although for now the bother shows in the negative. It will be revealed with Moshiach.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The seraphim above the man on the chair

blocks.text: This third level, really desiring to know G-d's essence even as the more one learns the more one sees it is beyond him, is the main vessel for the *chachma* and the secrets of the Torah. As the Sages say, the secrets of the Torah are given only to one whose heart is troubled within him.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: אבל כשהיה משיג לעצמות אור אין סוף ממש, שם הוא ענין השמחה בעצמותו
phrases.en: but were the person able to grasp G-d's essence, essence of the *Ohr Ein Sof*, then he would have this *simcha* in G-d's essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: ואף על פי שהוא גלוי העונג האלה״י הבא במורגש דווקא, אבל שרשו באמת בעצמות התענוג הנעלם, שממנו יצא היפוכו שהוא הבכיה מהעדרו שהוא הפלאה והבדלה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: even though *simcha* is this idea of having a G-dly pleasure come in a very felt, tangible way, but that *simcha* really comes from this essential pleasure which is causing this opposite thing, that the fact that it bothers him, which is the fact that it's so beyond him.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כי ב' קווין הללו שקולין גם כן בשווה ממש
phrases.en: because these two polar opposites of the joy and the sorrow of either understanding or not grasping G-d's essence are also completely equal and balanced.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: דהיינו שלפי ערך כח עוצם וגודל התענוג שהיה מתענג בעצמות דוקא כשהיה משיגו ממש, כך ימצא כח היפוכו, שהוא הבכיה העמוקה כשלא יכילו כלי מוחו להשיג כנזכר לעיל ודי למבין.
phrases.en: That exactly according to how much pleasure and joy a person has in grasping G-d's essence, that causes this being troubled and crying and this deep sorrow from the person's inability to understand and grasp G-dliness. And that's enough to understand.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: A person's main intention should be to know G-d's *Atzmus*, His essence, but he should look to know Him through the world, what he can grasp. That is what the saying means that when a person davens his eyes are down and his heart is up. He wants the essence, but he looks at the handiwork. If he looks at the world and understands it, and his real desire is to know G-d Himself, a light of the essence can shine into the handiwork, and he can have the grasp of the essence in it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: A gift between two people who love each other is worth nothing compared with what it expresses, and both know it. Still, it is sincere, and something of the essence shines into the token. It shines only when one has the maturity not to value the gift itself, and is bothered that no better way exists to express what he means. That very bother, that the vessel is not good enough, is what allows the essence to shine into it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: That is the idea of *kisisa lemaor*, the crushing of the vessel, which the Rebbe describes in several places. No matter how much Torah and mitzvos a Jew does, nothing is great enough to give true praise to G-d. When he is bothered by that, the essential connection is revealed, and the essence shines into our *avoda*. What allows the essence to be there is the recognition that it is not good enough, and so I keep trying and growing.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Someone who thinks, "It's just this book of 54 chapters; I'll master it, and then I'm a big *tzaddik*," has a sense of accomplishment that is a *yesh*, and it fails to capture the essence. Someone who says, "It's beyond anything, so I'll do nothing," has no *kli* either. Put the two together: recognise it is beyond me, and therefore do what I can. In davening we say that even if we cannot praise G-d enough, we will use our mouths and limbs to praise Him as best we can. Humility makes what we have a vessel for the essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: These two opposites, joy and sorrow at grasping or not grasping the essence, are equal. The amount of pleasure a person has in the essence when he grasps it is exactly the depth of the crying when the mind cannot grasp it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: So this is the basic frame. There are three levels of *avoda*, corresponding to *bina*, *chachma*, and the essence, or *keser*, and in each there are two opposites. If a connection on a level is real, it brings both out: the feeling of being crushed and inadequate, which then lets the essence shine in.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

sections.title: The order of the levels: from revealed light to the hidden essence
sections.summary: The order runs from joy in G-dliness grasped, through the delight of the hidden *koach mah* of *chachma*, to the essential delight of the essence. At each level the opposite is a sorrow in proportion: the tears of a true friend, and the sense of being crushed in exile.

phrases.he: ונמצא סדר המדרגות בדבר והיפוכו כך הם,
phrases.en: the order of these different levels of having these two opposites, these different opposite expressions of a person's connection to G-dliness, follow this progression.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: חדוה ושמחה מגלוי אור אלה״י המושג ממש,
phrases.en: first, the first step is *chedva* and *simcha* from G-dliness revealed in a way that they can really grasp.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: והיפוכו יוצא בכיה בהסתר המנגד לזה
phrases.en: And this causes the opposite, that a person feels bothered and troubled, or sometimes even cry, from when there's a concealment

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: ולמעלה מזה בבחינת ענג וחדוה הנעלם שבכח מ''ה דחכמה בעצמות אלהו״ת המהווה כו',
phrases.en: higher than this, that a person has this deeper pleasure and joy that's in this more subconscious level that's coming from this direct perception that which is called *koach mah* of *chachma*, where a person senses the essence of G-dliness, which is the Creator itself, not just the creation, and a person feels connected to that.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: וכחו בהיפוכו יוצא למאוס בחייו ובחיי כל זולתו,
phrases.en: And what this causes is that a person despises their life; the simple translation is 'despises his life', but it means of a physical life that's empty of G-dliness. If it's not connected to G-dliness, on its own he doesn't value it, and even the life of anyone else.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כמו מי לי כו'
phrases.en: like it says, *mi li bashamayim*, like 'What is there for me in heavens?'

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: ולמעלה גם מזה הענג והחדוה העצמיים בעצמות אלהו״ת דוקא, כמו וישמחו בך ממש בגלוי כו'
phrases.en: and even higher than this is the essential pleasure and joy that comes from the very essence of G-dliness, like it says that we rejoice in You, when G-d's essence will be revealed.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כוחו בהיפוכו יוצא כאשר לא יכילו כלי מוחו להכיל כו', יבכה
phrases.en: and from its strength comes its opposite, when his mind cannot grasp it, then he cries.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: (וכמו בכיה דאוהב הנאמן בנפשו בהפרדו, כדוד ויהונתן דאהבת נפשו אהבו, דכתיב וישקו ויבכו כו'
phrases.en: and this is like the tears of a very deep, true friend who loves his friend like himself. When they separate, it's a very painful thing. Like when David and Jonathan were separated, it says they cried. And it says there, he loved him like himself.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: שבא מכח ריבוי אהבה בתענוג הגדול שביחודם ודבוקם כו' וכה"ג).
phrases.en: these tears come from their great love and the great pleasure they have from being united and being together.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The order of the levels is this: first, joy from G-dliness revealed in a form that can be grasped, the pride of an accomplishment: look how great it is, I did this mitzvah, I understood this. The opposite of that comes as tears when that revealed light is concealed, when a person cannot live openly G-dly, cannot do Torah and mitzvos in the open.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Higher still is a pleasure hidden in the *koach mah* of *chachma*: the delight of G-d's essence, the Creator Himself and not only what He creates. Its opposite is that a person loathes his life, and the life of everyone else, if it is not connected to G-dliness. Even the spiritual life of accomplishments he discards: he wants G-d's essence, not even *Gan Eden*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The student who does not care about the grade
blocks.text: Take a student who learns *lishmah*. He really wants to understand, and does not care about the grade; even the best grade is not what he is after.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Higher still is the essential delight and joy of G-d's essence, "we rejoice in You", openly, when His essence will be revealed. From its strength comes its opposite: when the mind cannot contain it, one cries.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The tears of a true friend, who loves his friend as himself, are like those of David and Jonathan, who kissed and cried when they were parted. They viewed themselves as one identity. Such a person's connection to G-d is not even a pleasure; it is his very essence, that he is one with G-d.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Those tears come from great love and the pleasure of being united, so separation causes great pain. This is the sense of being crushed in exile, which the Rebbe describes in *Ve'Atah Tetzaveh*: even when all is good, a person feels crushed as long as G-d's essence is not revealed. That comes from the third level, not from things being bad.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 049 ch 6 part 2.mp3

sections.title: The answer: joy reaches the essence, and the tears of exile prepare for it
sections.summary: The paradox is answered: the grasp is of a light that is a *tzimtzum* of G-d, but the joy's root reaches the essence. Then the chapter turns to the three stages of dissatisfaction, the joy of the redemption, and the tears of the present exile.

phrases.he: ובכ"ז מתורץ ענין הנזכר לעיל בשמחה שבבינה וענג שבחכמה,
phrases.en: Now we can answer our question about how the *simcha* is in *bina*, which only grasps the created external world and not G-d's essence, and pleasure is in *chachma*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: דגם שההשגה עצמה היא בבחינת צמצום אור האלה״י שמשיגו,
phrases.en: Even though what you are understanding is the way G-d limits Himself into the world, into forms that we can understand.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: אבל השמחה שרשה מגיע בעצמות אלהו״ת דוקא
phrases.en: But yet what the person is really enjoying, even though you are understanding and seeing G-d's handiwork, you are appreciating that for its connection to G-d's essence. And so the *simcha* really is in G-d's essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: כמו הנשמות נהנין מזיו השכינה ממש בגן עדן
phrases.en: Like it says, that the souls enjoy the ray of the *Shechinah* in *Gan Eden*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: גם השגתם באה על ידי צמצום כידוע
phrases.en: Even in *Gan Eden*, even when the soul is outside the body, even the highest understanding, even the highest *tzaddik* who has been in the highest level of *Gan Eden* for thousands of years, no matter how refined the understanding is, is still not capturing G-d's essence in its entirety. Like it says, 'in chachma You made them all': even the *chachma* of *Atzilus* is like the physical *Asiya*, a very limited construct compared to His essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: וזהו וישמחו בך דוקא,
phrases.en: This is the idea that it says, that we will rejoice in You, specifically in G-d's essence, not in just a limited form.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: והיינו חדווא בסטרא דא ובכיה היפוכה יוצא מכחה
phrases.en: It says also in the *Zohar* that I have the sorrow or the tears on one side of my heart and the joy on the other side of my heart, or he says the other way, the joy on one side and the tears on the other.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: בג' מיני מדריגות הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: And that, like we said, there are three stages of relating: first being pained by not having the understanding in *bina*, then understanding it in a tangible way; then a person is pained that they don't appreciate G-d's transcendence, and then they have the joy of recognising G-d's transcendence; and then they have the pain of not being able to grasp G-d's essence, and then the joy of being able to bring that down into their understanding, their *avoda*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: וב' קווין שקולין הם בשווה ממש כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: Like we said, these are two equal poles of the same, two sides of the same coin, and the fact that it bothers a person shows that they're connected to it, and their desire is attached there.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: The class opens with a recap of the question and the ground for its answer. The paradox is that "they will rejoice in You" sits beside the *bittul* that comes from *chachma*. *Chassidus* teaches a level of service motivated by measurable results, a limited ray of the *Shechinah*. The real essence of the *Shechinah* is reached through *teshuva*: a bitterness and dissatisfaction, a feeling that nothing I do is great enough, which leads to service full of *chayus*. The same idea is in *pshat*, *remez*, *drash* and *sod*, which *Chassidus* wears as garments, changed to show that the essence transcends each one.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Recap of the question and the grounds for the answer, from the start of class 050; placed before line 52, where the answer is given.

blocks.text: A person limited to one approach, learning or *davenen* or *chesed*, is not connected to G-d's essence. Flexibility, even doing the opposite of one's nature, as Abraham at the *Akeidah* acted in *gevura*, shows that one's commitment is to the essence beyond any form. Then *bittul* is joined to striving: nothing I do is great enough, yet I keep doing my best and never feel I have arrived. That becomes a vessel for the transcendent essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Recap from the start of class 050, placed before line 52.

blocks.text: Life is growth and motion, and cannot be captured in a still form. Understand the creation, and be aware of how G-d transcends it: then the constant change is itself an expression of the transcendence. Scientific and kabbalistic concepts are models, garments that are flexible; they never capture the essence. Hold to faith that transcends understanding, and plug it into the understanding. We do not have Him in our back pocket. Once we have that humility, He can be captured in the very same ideas.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Recap from the start of class 050, placed before line 52.

blocks.text: The question: *simcha* seems to be in *bina*, which grasps only the created world, and pleasure in *chachma*. But perceiving G-d's transcendence through *chachma* gives *bittul*, so how can there be *simcha* in His essence? The answer: even what one grasps is the way G-d limits Himself into forms we can understand, and yet the root of the joy reaches His essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: In the *maamar* *Yafeh Sha'a Achas*, *teshuva* is the sense that G-d transcends everything, and *maasim tovim* bring that awareness into action, so that the actions become good and are enlightened with a deeper light. First comes *teshuva*, then that sense is brought into one's understanding of the world.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: Even while a person understands G-d's handiwork, what he is really enjoying is his appreciation of it for its connection to G-d's essence. So the joy really is in the essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: Souls in *Gan Eden* enjoy the ray of the *Shechinah*, but even their grasp comes through *tzimtzum*. Even the highest *tzaddik* in the highest level of *Gan Eden* does not capture G-d's essence in its entirety: as it says, "in chachma You made them all", even the *chachma* of *Atzilus* is like the physical *Asiya*, a limited construct before His essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: This is "they will rejoice in You" specifically, in the essence and not in a limited form. The *Zohar* says that the sorrow and the tears sit on one side of the heart and the joy on the other, or the other way round. There are three stages: first the pain of not having the understanding of *bina*, then grasping it in a tangible way; then the pain at not appreciating G-d's transcendence, and the joy of recognising it; then the pain at not grasping the essence, and the joy of bringing it down into one's *avoda*. The two poles are equal, so the pain itself shows that a person is connected to it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: וזהו בשמחה ובטוב לבב מרוב כל, בהשגת המהוה
phrases.en: This is the idea that a person has this great joy and pleasure and gladness in knowing G-d that transcends everything, like the *pasuk* says, that you should rejoice in serving G-d. The simple meaning is from the abundance of all the blessings G-d gives us, but the way it's explained in *Chassidus* is from how G-d transcends everything within creation.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: וכמו לעתיד דכתיב עין בעין נראה כו'
phrases.en: Like it says, in the time to come, "eye to eye", that we're going to see G-d eye to eye.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: ואמר ביום ההוא הנה אלהינ״ו זה,
phrases.en: And we will say on that day, "behold, this is our G-d"; and whenever it uses the word *zeh*, that implies you're looking and pointing at something in front of you.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: לנוכח,
אז נגילה ונשמחה בו דווקא
phrases.en: Then, it says, once a person has that recognition, they will rejoice and have this *simcha*, this celebration in knowing G-d Himself, specifically.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: כידוע ודי למבין
phrases.en: It is enough for the understanding.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: אבל עכשיו כל זה בוקע ויוצא על ידי המנגד, היפוכו דוקא, שהוא הבכיה מסטרא דא
phrases.en: But now, in the time of *galus*, whether globally or personally, when a person doesn't yet have that perspective, the way to attach to it and start planting the seed of this deeper perspective is by feeling uncomfortable with *galus*, by not being accepting, not being comfortable with an understanding, and having this sense, "No, that's not good enough."

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: עד רום המעלות
וכמו שכתוב בבכי יבואו דוקא,
phrases.en: Like it says, with tears we will come to *Moshiach*; it is specifically through being dissatisfied with the *galus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: וכן הלוך ילך ובכה כו'
phrases.en: It says also, we're going to walk along while crying towards the *geulah*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: ולעתיד לבא יהיה השחוק
phrases.en: And in the future comes the joy, and also we could start experiencing it now, sometimes, the idea of *yimot HaMoshiach*: that we should start actually experiencing that joy and *taanug* of *Moshiach* now.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אז ימלא שחוק פינו
phrases.en: Like it says, then our mouth will be filled with laughter; in the times of *Moshiach*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין הקניגיא כו'
phrases.en: Like it explains about the joust that G-d is going to arrange between the *shor habar* and the *leviathan* in the times of *Moshiach*, which is going to bring this great pleasure to the *tzaddikim*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב כי אתה אבינו, זה יצחק, שצחוק זה בא לעתיד מן המנגד שלו, אשר בחינת הבכיה היה בגלות כידוע.
phrases.en: And this is what it says, "for You are our father", that it refers to *Yitzchak*, the three *avos*: when *Moshiach* comes we will mainly focus on the idea of *Yitzchak*, which is *tzchok*, laughter, and that laughter comes in the future as a result of our dissatisfaction and the tears and the sorrow of the time of *galus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: The joy of knowing G-d beyond everything is the great joy: the revelation of the essence within the world, which is the level of *geulah*, personal and general. "In the future we shall see eye to eye," and then, "behold, this is our G-d." The word *zeh* points at what is in front of you. Creation from nothing is a fundamental idea in Judaism: the world need not be the way it is. It is only this way by G-d's choice, an expression of the *Ein Sof* and of His infinite ability to do whatever He wants.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: Then, with our physical sight and all our other senses, we change how we appreciate what we see: we realize that we are looking at G-d and experiencing Him. Then we rejoice in knowing G-d Himself, specifically. Once we recognise that G-d transcends any form, it is a kind of paradox, and then we can see G-d within the physical world.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

sensitivity.publishable: The classic *din* in *halacha*: a person who holds up a brick and says, "This is my G-d," has committed *avoda zara*. The physical object is his first premise, a limited thing; then he attaches G-d to it, confining Him to that, and that is not true, so it is *avoda zara*.

sensitivity.publishable: Pantheism, claiming the whole universe as G-d, is also *avoda zara*, which is why we say the entire universe is created from nothing. And the view of Aristotle and others, that the universe always existed, with matter that G-d forms as a soul forms a body, is against the fundamental idea of Jewish monotheism too. All of reality is transcendent in its inherent nature: even time and space need not exist; they are created from nothing.
