blocks.text: Once we recognise that G-d's essence transcends all these things, we see G-d choosing to create this reality. When I point at a thing and say, "This is G-d," I am not limiting G-d to it; I am widening my view of it. That is *re'iyas hamehus*, seeing G-d's essence in the physical world.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: But now, in exile, when a person does not yet have that perspective, the way to plant the seed is to feel uncomfortable with exile and not accept an understanding, saying, "No, that's not good enough." He recalls, as a small child, guessing to a friend about G-d; the friend's faith rejected any boxing G-d in or describing Him physically. That is the first step, the sense of humility and discomfort at the limits of our understanding, and it is what will later open a person to the correct understanding.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: This first tear is a sense of *teshuva*, feeling far from G-d and wanting to come close. As Rosh Hashanah approaches, the Rebbe's *shofar gadol*, the great *shofar* of *Moshiach*, is the feeling that by nature we are far from G-d, however many mitzvos we do, because His essence is so great that nothing can approach it, and so we are all outcasts. The small *shofar* is being upset at not yet doing something tangible, and feeling that once I get there, I'll have arrived. The great *shofar* unites all of humanity: all equally far from G-d, all trying to grow. The real essence of one's G-dly connection is the constant wish to grow, not any particular accomplishment.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.title: The Frierdiker Rebbe in Philadelphia
blocks.text: The Frierdiker Rebbe, on what he believes was his first trip to America, was seeing people in what he thinks was Philadelphia. Three men came in to challenge him: "What business do you have coming here and telling us what to do? And what do you know about America? You're just this old European rabbi." He had them brought in at once, ahead of the people who had come for blessings. He told them he gives a blessing for health, though he isn't a doctor, and for a livelihood, though he isn't a businessman, and that the question of what right he has to demand Torah and mitzvos in America is one he must answer, or what is he? What did he want from them? "There are 613 mitzvos, and I can't do all of them. Try to do what you can."

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: This deeper perspective captures the real essence, the great *shofar*. The deeper sense of inadequacy is what lets us, in time, capture G-d's essence in our *avoda* and in our understanding.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: Like it says, "with tears they will come": it is specifically through being dissatisfied with the *galus* that we come to *Moshiach*. The sense of *ad matai*, how long, propels us to the joy of the *geulah*. It says also, "we will walk along while crying," towards the *geulah*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: In the future the joy comes too, and we can start experiencing it now, the idea of *yimot HaMoshiach*: we should start actually having that joy and *taanug* of *Moshiach* now. It can be tasted now, the way one tastes the Shabbos food on Friday, and the Rebbe more and more emphasises the joy. Yet both sides must go together. Joy without being bothered by exile is fake joy. Being bothered without taking up the chance to learn *Chassidus* and do Torah shows that one is not really sorry.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: The joust that G-d will arrange in the time of *Moshiach* between the *shor habar* and the *leviathan* gives great pleasure to the *tzaddikim*. The *shor habar* is the service of the body, the physical mitzvos. The *leviathan* is inner *avoda*: contemplation, *kabbalah*, *Chassidus*, and the duties of the heart. Each thinks it is the main thing. Each is inadequate, and each elevates the other to a higher point, which reveals the deeper joy in G-d's essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: "For You are our father," we say, and that refers to *Yitzchak*, the laughter of the future, which comes from the tears of exile. It should come by good means, through *avoda*. That is the idea of Elul: a *cheshbon hanefesh* on why we are here, what our *neshama* is, what gifts we were given, and feeling inadequate about living up to it. Then we attain this in a positive way and are spared the troubles that would otherwise bring it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

sections.title: Tikun chatzos: the tears that prepare prayer
sections.summary: Tears at midnight over the distance from G-d, and the sense of responsibility for one's own soul, prepare a person for prayer. Simple tears for sins, sincerely meant, are bread for the soul and fix the root of the blemish.

phrases.he: ובכל זה יובן טעם האמיתי לענין תיקון חצות בבכיה דוקא
phrases.en: This is the real purpose of *tikun chatzos*, which in previous generations was a very common custom, especially among those who practiced *kabbalah* and studied the inner parts of Torah: they would wake at midnight and cry over the destruction of the *Beis HaMikdash*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: שהוא תועלת לנפש להיות בתפילה גילוי תענוג העצמי, כמו וישמחו בך וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: Having this sense of this inadequacy in *tikun chatzos* over a person's own soul not living up to its potential, that is what allows a person then, when they *daven* the next morning and in general throughout the day, to have this true revelation of G-dliness and have a true *taanug* and sense of G-dly pleasure and feel that they're connected to G-d.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: והגם שהבכיה בתיקון חצות הוא דמעות פשוטים על חטאות נעורים וכהאי גוונא,
phrases.en: In general, *tikun chatzos* is just simple tears for a person's sins. It doesn't seem to be necessarily this deeper idea of wanting to understand G-d; it's more just simple *teshuva*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: אבל על זה אמר היתה לי דמעתי לחם יומם ולילה
phrases.en: About this it says that my tears were like bread for me by day and by night.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: The true reason for *tikun chatzos* is that in previous generations it was a common custom, especially among those who learned the inner parts of the Torah, to wake at midnight and cry over the destruction of the *Beis HaMikdash*. The *Siddur im Dach* and the Mitteler Rebbe's *maamarim* explain it as mainly a person thinking about his soul: that he has a piece of G-d inside him and a spark of the *Shechinah*, and asking whether he is living up to who he really is and his real purpose. That inner sorrow is a personal *galus*; it is the deeper level of fear of G-d called the fear of *bushah*, a sense of embarrassment at not being true to oneself. It brings a person to a personal *geulah*, and when he frees his own spark, that helps bring the general *geulah*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: This sorrow prepares the soul to be in prayer, with a true revelation of the delight in G-dliness, as in "they will rejoice in You": a taste of the joy of the *geulah* in one's *davenen*, like aged wine. There are two main ways to reach it: this kind of reckoning, or giving *tzedakah* with self-sacrifice, or *mesirus nefesh* for *ahavas Yisroel*. Those are also ways of connecting on that level, in action.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: *Tikun chatzos* is usually simply tears for one's sins, and seemingly it is not the deeper wish to understand G-d. The same is true of Elul, Tishrei, Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur: seemingly they are *teshuva* for our mistakes, not so much for not being able to grasp G-d's essence. Yet even the simplest tears of a simple person for a simple sin come from this place: he really wants to be connected to G-d. Those tears become bread, a source of vitality, when he says *Shema* and davens morning and evening.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: בקריאת שמע ותפילה דשחרית וערבית כו'
phrases.en: When he says *Shema* and davens morning and evening.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: מפני שהדמעות על הריחוק שלו מעוונות וחטאים שלו מתקנים בחינת מקור הפגם,
phrases.en: Because these tears a person has for being distant from G-d, even if it's just because of simple sins, are fixing the general source.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: שהוא דוקא פריקות עול מלכות שמים,
phrases.en: The whole reason that their soul is disconnected from G-d is that they have this casting off of the yoke, this lack of sense of responsibility and duty to G-d.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: ובחינת גלות השכינה הוא בא בדרך פרט בכל ניצוץ אלה״י
phrases.en: And that's the idea of the personal *galus* of the *Shechinah*, the *galus* of the divine presence in each individual soul.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: והדמעה הזאת תתקן ותעביר הפגם לגמרי
phrases.en: And so these tears totally wipe away and remove that blemish.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: ותעורר למעלה בחינת הבכיה שמנגד ובא מכח היפוכו, שהוא החדוה העצמית הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: And so these tears awaken above the opposite of the tears, which is this essential joy.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: להאיר בנפשו האלהי״ת בקריאת שמע ותפילה כו'
phrases.en: And this is what enlightens a person's G-dly soul when they say *Shema* and daven, which includes the whole idea of learning *Chassidus*, of studying and contemplating G-dliness.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: להיות ממש כמו לחם לנפשו כו'
phrases.en: And it becomes literally like food for the soul; it really strengthens the person's G-dly soul, wakes it up, and gives it the strength and vitality that it needs.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: ולהיפוך בפריקות עול, היפך הדמעה, כמו והתברך בלבבו בשרירות לבי אלך כו'
phrases.en: The opposite of the tears is casting off the yoke, like the verse: they bless themselves saying, "I'll do whatever I want," without any sense of duty.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: כעבד שמורד,
phrases.en: Like a rebellious servant.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

phrases.he: שהמרידה ופריקות עול עיקר ומקור לכל שיעשה נגד רצון האדון כו':
phrases.en: And this casting off of the yoke is whatever particular things that the servant is doing against his master, rebelling in this or that.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: When he says *Shema* and davens morning and evening, this is what fuels the deeper experience of G-d's essence and opens his eyes to G-dliness all day. The tears of distance, even over simple sins, fix the general source of the blemish, which is the casting off of the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: The whole reason a soul is cut off from G-d is that it casts off the yoke, lacks a sense of duty and responsibility to G-d, and loses the awareness that it is here with a mission and was given gifts for a reason. Having that duty to live up to its true G-dly nature is the personal exile of the *Shechinah*, the exile of the divine presence in each individual soul.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: These tears wipe out the blemish completely and awaken above the opposite of tears, which is the essential joy. That joy opens the person to deeper understanding and to seeing G-dliness in a deeper way, and it needs a connection to G-d's essence, which begins with feeling far from G-d and being upset about it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: For that activity to really enlighten the soul, when one says *Shema* and davens, and when one learns *Chassidus* and contemplates G-dliness, it first requires this preparation and this connection to G-d's essence. Then it becomes literally food for the soul: it strengthens the G-dly soul, wakes it up, and gives it the strength and vitality it needs.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: The opposite of the tears is the casting off of the yoke, like the servant who rebels. Rebellion is the root of whatever is done against the master's will. The main problem is not the mistake, which a human makes, but the lack of good intention: "I don't have to listen, I can do what I want." The cure is to recognise a duty, do one's best to fulfil one's mission, and keep trying to improve. That feeling of being human and inadequate is itself healthy, and it should motivate a person to grow.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

blocks.text: The class stops here, because the rest is a short *kitzur* of *Derech Chaim* at the end of the chapter, the whole topic of *teshuva*. The Mitteler Rebbe has three books that discuss it at great length, *Shaar HaTeshuva* and *Shaar HaTefila* among them; this is a quick overview of the idea.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 050 ch 6 part 3.mp3

sections.title: Turning from the bad: the root of sin is casting off the yoke, not the single sin
sections.summary: The chapter closes on the root of sin: casting off the yoke, a rebellion that shows in small choices. Tears for particular sins do not fix it; a sense of mission does. Whoever has joy in G-d and sorrow at distance from Him must keep both, and then his learning does not go to waste.

phrases.he: והנה על זה אמר אוילים מדרך פשעם. פשעים אלו המרדים בפריקת עול, גם שיתענו מעונותיהם בחטאות נעורים, מה יועיל, כי כל אוכל דחכמה הנזכר לעיל תתעב נפשם
phrases.en: These are the rebellious people, people who rebel by casting off the yoke, having a lack of sense of responsibility and duty. Even though they afflict themselves and fast over their particular sins, it doesn't help, because they despise any food: their souls despise this food of *chachma*, that they don't want to learn about G-dliness and *chasidus* in general.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

phrases.he: היפך הענג שחיה תחיה לנפשו כו'
phrases.en: And so this is the opposite of having this pleasure in G-dliness, which would bring life to the soul.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב ויגיעו עד שערי מות כמו שכתוב החיים והטוב,
phrases.en: And this is what it says: such people will reach the gate of death, without change, without doing *teshuva*. Like it says, "behold I place before you life and good, death and bad, and choose life."

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

phrases.he: שהוא שמחה וטוב לב בענג העצמי הנזכר לעיל, והיפוכו מות ורע בפריקת עול
phrases.en: So a person has to choose the opposite, which is this life and good. A person has to cultivate this connection, and this sense that their true joy and their true happiness is in this essential desire to know G-d. If a person doesn't do that, then even if he does Torah and mitzvos on one of the lower levels of motivation, it can get dragged down into *kelipah* and eventually fall down. The opposite of having that connection to G-dliness in this way is death and bad, casting off the yoke of heaven.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.text: Class 051 picks up the tears of *tikun chatzos* from the last class. He recaps the three stages: first the *bina* that grasps the concrete expressions of G-dliness in the world; then the feeling that this is not enough, and the *chachma* that recognizes how the Creator transcends the world; then the third level, wanting G-d's essence brought down into the world in a tangible way. That deepest dissatisfaction is connected to the great *shofar* of *Moshiach*. When the essence is actually revealed, there is true joy in *hisbonenus*, in seeing G-d's essence within the world, and that is ultimately the revelation of *Moshiach* and the *geulah*. Before davening one thinks about one's sins, the *galus* of the *Shechinah*, and how far one is from the potential of one's soul; that sense of distance prepares prayer. The same is done in Elul, on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, and when we say *tachanun*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Recap from the start of class 051, which picks up the tears of tikun chatzos from the previous class; placed before line 72, where the class resumes reading.

blocks.text: He goes back to where the last class ended. The real source of sin is *prikas ol*, the lack of a sense of duty and responsibility to G-d, and its repair is *kabbalas ol*, the sense of mission and purpose. The Frierdiker Rebbe, in *Likutei Dibburim*, says that a person who asks himself five questions turns on his soul: why did G-d put me in this world, what unique gifts did He give me, what could I accomplish with them for myself, what could I accomplish to help others, and what am I actually doing to make that happen. That is the *cheshbon hanefesh* that brings *kabbalas ol*. *Kabbalas ol* is more than listening to what one is told. It is responsibility and mission, so that a person does it whether he likes it or not, because it is more important than just himself.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Recap from the start of class 051, which picks up the tears of tikun chatzos; placed before line 72, where the class resumes.

blocks.text: He explains the verse from Psalms that line 72 quotes: the wicked stumble from the way of their *pesha*, and their sins afflict them. Hebrew has three words for sin. *Chet* is a mistake, a lack, not necessarily malicious. *Avon* is a perversion, more intentional, a localized problem with one *midda*. *Pesha* is rebellion, a fundamental problem of refusing the whole idea of serving G-d and fulfilling one's mission. The small choices that look unimportant, what psychology calls SUDs, seemingly unimportant decisions, show a person's priorities, and they add up to *prikas ol*, the source of the problems. When there is no logical reason to pick one over the other, the choice shows whether a person has a sense of duty, or is saying, 'I can just do what I want.' When the teacher was a yeshiva student, after Pesach he lacked motivation until a *chavrusa* told him to come exactly on time. It turned things around, because that small choice reflected his priorities.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Explains the words of line 72 before the class reads that line; placed before line 72.

blocks.text: The *poshim*, the rebels who cast off the yoke, afflict themselves and fast over particular sins, and that does not help. Their root problem is the rebellion, and so their souls despise the food of *chachma*: they don't want to learn about G-dliness and *chasidus*. If a person fasts and says he is sorry for sinning, but does not connect positively to G-d and deepen the connection, he will sin again. Even a lot of learning does not fix the source if it lacks the humility and *bittul* that come from *chachma*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.text: The opposite of the pleasure that gives life is a soul that never connects to G-dliness as its true identity. Without that, a person is always fighting uphill, like going up a down escalator, and he will never succeed in the long run. The *Baal Shem Tov* taught that Torah and mitzvos cannot be done only because one has to. They must be felt as who one is, and then done with *chayus*, with joy and pleasure, and appreciation of the connection to G-dliness. Without that essential idea, a person keeps stumbling into the same things.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.text: The verse says the wicked reach the gates of death: they do not do *teshuva*. Choose life, which is joy and good heart in the essential pleasure described above. One has to work to develop that connection. If a person does not, then even when he does Torah and mitzvos on the lower motives, they are dragged into *kelipah* and fall. That is what is meant by the opposite, death and bad, in casting off the yoke. This is why even simple tears and simple *teshuva* for sins can really connect a person to the essence of G-dliness: it is all one thing.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

phrases.he: והדמעה בתיקון חצות דווקא הוא עיקר ההכנה בנפשו להיות בתפלה כל ענין הנזכר לעיל בג' מדריגות דבכיה מסטרא דא כו'
phrases.en: And this is why this type of tears of *tikun chatzos*, when a person thinks about what his real mission is, and whether his G-dly soul, a spark of the *Shechinah*, is really living up to its mission and potential, and is bothered by that, is what really prepares a person to be successful in his *davening* and his *hisbonenus* and learning of G-dliness, with these three stages of sorrow and joy that we talked about.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

phrases.he: ואם לא, יטעה את עצמו באחד מאלה, או בכיה לבד וחדווה לבד או שאינם לאמיתתן ולעומקן
phrases.en: If a person doesn't make this preparation, he is going to fool himself and be deluded in one of these two ways: either just the sorrow, or just the joy. Or they'll have both, but they're not true, they're not real, they're not really deep.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

phrases.he: והרי זה סימן שלא נגע על נפשו אור האלה״י, רק מרחוק מאד, כמו בסוד גלות השכינה בכללות נשמות ישראל
phrases.en: If a person doesn't have both of these feelings in a true, deep way, that's the sign that his connection to G-dliness is not really reaching his soul. He views it as a far-off thing, separate from him. The whole thing we're trying to feel is that this is really who I am: a literally little piece of G-d from above. This is my true nature, and so I have to live up to it; my real self is to be a G-dly being, connected to G-dliness. This is similar to the general *galus* of the *Shechinah* for all the Jewish people, but on a personal level, if I'm not turning on that G-dly spark, that is a personal *galus* of the spark of the *Shechinah* in myself.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

phrases.he: (וזהו עיקר ומקור הסיבה הכללית לכל הנופלים תמיד ממדריגתם בעונג וחדוה האלהי״ת בלתי מתקיימת כלל וכלל
phrases.en: This is the main reason why you find that sometimes people learn *chasidus*, and they come to *farbrengen*, get very inspired, and then it goes away, and they end up falling into problems. It does not make a lasting impact on them.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.text: The tears of *tikun chatzos* are the main preparation for *davening*, *hisbonenus* and learning, with the three stages of sorrow and joy. This kind of tears comes from thinking about one's real mission: one's G-dly soul is a spark of the *Shechinah*, and the question is whether one is living up to that mission and potential. Being bothered by that is what prepares a person to succeed in his *davening*, in *hisbonenus*, and in learning about G-dliness, with those three stages.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.text: If the preparation is not made, a person fools himself: sorrow alone, beating himself up and then giving up, or joy alone, "it doesn't matter what I do, G-d loves me". Either way he does not progress. Or he has both, but they are not true or deep.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.text: Such a person's connection to G-dliness has not touched his soul. He views it as far off, separate from him. What is needed is the feeling that this is really who I am, a literal piece of G-d from above, and so I have to live up to that. The general exile of the *Shechinah* in Israel is mirrored in the personal exile of the spark in each of us.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.text: The main reason people fall from their level is that they learn *chasidus* and become inspired, and then the inspiration goes away and they fall into problems. It does not make a lasting impression. Everyone has ups and downs and learns from his mistakes. But being turned on in general, growing and making mistakes and getting up, is different from being turned on and then turned off.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

phrases.he: ובמעט מונעים מנגדים, ינתקו חבלי התקשרות מלבו לגמרי כנזכר לעיל, כמו שכתוב אוילים מדרך פשעם כו'
phrases.en: And that sometimes it can, like we mentioned before: a person could learn a lot of *chasidus* and *daven* and this kind of thing, but then they have a little bit of opposition, a little bit of disturbance, and they get disconnected from it, and they get distracted from it completely. So, like it says, they're stumbling from their way of their rebellion.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

phrases.he: כל אוכל כו' ולזה כל אשר קרבת אלהי״ם יחפץ באמת, יעשה הכנה רבה בנפשו תמיד בתיקון חצות ובענין בכיה מסטרא דא כו' הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: That leads to: they despise the food for their soul, this learning of *chasidus* and the *avodah*, and they lose their taste for it. And this is why anyone who truly desires to be close to G-d with truth will constantly make this preparation of *tikun chatzos*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

phrases.he: ולא יטעה את עצמו לאבד את נפשו בחנם ממש ודי למבין)
phrases.en: Then he will not fool himself, he won't be deluded, and everything he does will be real and true; and why should a person destroy their soul over nothing?

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

phrases.he: (ובכל זה יובן גם כן עיקר הטעם לענין הכלל הגדול בשם הרב המגיד זכרונו לברכה במרה שחורה הטבעית, שהוא כלי הכנה לעונג האמיתי במסירת נפש באחד כו' ולקבלת כל רזין כו' כמו שכתוב בקונטרס באריכות ודי למבין):
phrases.en: This also explains the great principle taught in the name of the Maggid of Mezeritch, about the natural black bile: when a person is naturally feeling down or sad, he should use that to think about *teshuva* and re-channel it, as the Tanya says in many places, to break the *kelipah* and motivate us in our *avodas Hashem*. That is a vessel to receive the true joy of G-dliness, and to be able to receive all the secrets of the Torah, like it's explained in another place at length.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.text: A person can learn a lot of *chasidus* and *daven*, and a little opposition or disturbance still cuts the attachment: he gets disconnected from it, and distracted from it completely. As the verse says, they stumble from their way of rebellion, and they despise the food of their soul; they lose their taste for this learning and *avodah*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.text: Whoever truly desires to be close to G-d makes constant preparation through *tikun chatzos* or, nowadays, by setting aside regular times to think about the questions: what is my soul, what is my mission and purpose, why did I come down here, what gifts did G-d give me, what could I accomplish with them for myself and for others, and what am I actually doing about it. That is what keeps a person awake and turned on, and gives him a sense of responsibility to live up to who he really is, not because it is the rule, but because it is his very nature. Doing so also helps him understand the learning better. Another route is *mesirus nefesh* for *ahavas Yisroel*, which the Alter Rebbe always talks about as refining the mind and heart a thousandfold. By connecting to another person and seeing his essential value, one is willing to sacrifice to help him, and that unlocks and uncovers one's own G-dly spark, so one is more easily turned on. It all goes hand in hand.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.text: Then he will not fool himself, and everything he does will be real and true, so he does not lose his soul for nothing. A person who is this close and connected has all these gifts, and the *chasidus* the Rebbe gave us; if he learns it and does it right, it won't be for nothing.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.text: This also explains a great principle taught in the name of the Maggid of Mezeritch, about the natural black bile, which is a person's natural sadness or low mood.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.text: When a person is naturally feeling down or sad, he should use that to think about *teshuva*, and to re-channel it, as the Tanya says in many places, to break the *kelipah* and to motivate us in our *avodas Hashem*.

blocks.text: That sense of dissatisfaction with our state and our exile is a good vessel, a tool and a receptacle for the true joy of G-dliness, and for being able to understand and receive all the secrets of the Torah, as it is explained at length in another place.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 06/Shaar HaYichud 051 ch 6 part 4.mp3

blocks.text: Approach the whole chapter, and the learning, with humility, not as an ego trip of becoming a holy kabbalist or getting special powers. Come to it with the sense of having a G-dly spark and wanting to live up to it, to be true to oneself, to do the most one can in one's personal mission, and to help others bring out their own G-dly potential. That is the real reason to learn, and it has to motivate us. Learned with that intention, it is understood properly. Rabbi Akiva entered *Pardes* in peace and came out in peace, because he went in intending to see how the knowledge could benefit the world and people.
